title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models
why_read: A new concept-attribution method for explaining black-box vision models that avoids needing model weights or large labeled datasets is a useful practical interpretability tool.
analysis: Hide and Seek (HnS) is an interpretability technique that explains vision model predictions using human-understandable concepts, like 'wears glasses' or 'has grass', without needing access to the model's internal weights. It works by finding images matching a concept, locating and masking that concept region, then checking how much the model's output changes, which gives a measure of how much that concept influenced the decision. The method is validated on face attribute (CelebA) and scene segmentation (COCO-Stuff) datasets and extends to tasks like captioning and satellite imagery where prior concept-attribution tools didn't apply. This matters because black-box interpretability tools that only need API-level access are more broadly usable in real deployments where model internals are proprietary.
